subject: paediatrics
title: Exclusive Breastfeeding, Milk Biology and Reflexes

steps.tx: Optimal infant nutrition during early life establishes immune protection and metabolic programming. The global standard of **exclusive breastfeeding** mandates providing solely breast milk to the infant with no supplementary liquids, water, or solids for the first six completed months (180 days) of life, allowing only oral rehydration salts, vitamins, minerals, and essential medications. Exclusive breastfeeding significantly lowers infant mortality from diarrhoeal illness and acute respiratory infections.
steps.say: Exclusive breastfeeding provides solely breast milk for the first six completed months, without supplementary water or food. It protects against infant mortality from diarrhoea and pneumonia.

vis.alt: Phases of human breast milk production and comparative biochemical composition.
vis.caption: Phases of human breast milk production and comparative biochemical composition.

steps.tx: The initial secretion from the mammary glands provides targeted biological defence. Secreted during the first three to four days following birth, **human colostrum** is a thick, yellowish fluid exceptionally rich in secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA), lactoferrin, lysozyme, and living maternal macrophages. Colostrum serves as the newborn's first natural immunization, coating the immature intestinal mucosa to prevent microbial adhesion while facilitating meconium evacuation through mild laxative properties.
steps.say: Colostrum is secreted during the first three days postpartum. Packed with secretory IgA, lactoferrin, and leukocytes, it lines the neonatal gut to prevent bacterial invasion and promotes meconium passage.

steps.tx: Compositional changes during an individual nursing session fulfill both hydration and energetic requirements. At the initiation of feeding, watery foremilk provides abundant volumes of lactose and water to satisfy the infant's thirst. As nursing proceeds, the lipid concentration rises markedly, yielding rich **hindmilk secretion** that supplies high calorie density and vital essential fatty acids, creating satiety and promoting healthy weight gain.
steps.say: Foremilk is released first, offering lactose and water to quench thirst. Hindmilk emerges toward the end of the feed, rich in fats and calories to promote satiety and steady weight gain.

left.title: Foremilk Properties
points: High water content, rich in lactose and soluble proteins

right.title: Hindmilk Properties
points: Up to 4-5 times higher lipid concentration

steps.tx: Sensory stimulation of the areola coordinates two complementary neuroendocrine pathways. Infant suckling triggers the anterior pituitary **prolactin reflex**, also known as the milk secretion reflex, stimulating alveolar epithelial cells to synthesize and secrete milk into the lumen. Prolactin levels surge during each feed and are highest at night, making nighttime breastfeeding especially important for maintaining maternal milk supply.
steps.say: Suckling stimulates prolactin release from the anterior pituitary, commanding alveolar cells to make milk. Nocturnal prolactin spikes make nighttime nursing crucial for sustaining supply.

rows: Inhibited by maternal pain and anxiety

steps.tx: Active ejection of synthesized milk requires neurohypophyseal activation. The **let-down reflex**, mediated by oxytocin released from the posterior pituitary, stimulates contraction of myoepithelial cells encircling the mammary alveoli, forcing milk through the lactiferous ducts into the ampullae. Unlike prolactin, the oxytocin let-down reflex is readily influenced by maternal emotion, being suppressed by anxiety, fatigue, and pain, but triggered by seeing or hearing the baby.
steps.say: Oxytocin from the posterior pituitary triggers the let-down reflex, contracting myoepithelial cells to expel milk. Stress or pain inhibits this reflex, while maternal relaxation aids ejection.

left.title: Oxytocin Facilitators
points: Skin-to-skin kangaroo contact, seeing baby photograph, hearing infant cry, warm breast compresses, confidence

right.title: Oxytocin Inhibitors
points: Severe pain from cracked nipples, psychological anxiety, exhaustion, doubt regarding milk volume adequacy

steps.tx: Macronutrient ratios in human milk reflect specific evolutionary adaptations for human neurological growth. Human milk contains roughly 1.0 gram of **whey and casein** protein per 100 millilitres with a delicate 60:40 whey-to-casein ratio that forms soft, easily digestible curd in the infant stomach. In contrast, unmodified cow milk contains 3.3 grams of protein per 100 millilitres dominated by hard 20:80 casein curd, placing excessive solute load on immature neonatal kidneys.
steps.say: Human milk contains a 60:40 whey to casein ratio that forms light, easily digested curds. Cow milk has a 20:80 ratio with hard curds and high protein, overloading neonatal kidneys.

rows: Cow milk causes high renal solute load
Human milk digests rapidly in 90 min
Crucial for retina and brain myelin
Human milk protects from iron deficiency

steps.tx: Proper biomechanical positioning at the breast prevents maternal pain and ensures efficient milk transfer. Effective **breast attachment** requires four objective WHO clinical signs: the infant's mouth is wide open, the lower lip is turned outwards (everted), the infant's chin touches the maternal breast, and more of the dark areola is visible above the upper lip than below the lower lip. Poor attachment causes painful cracked nipples and inadequate milk transfer.
steps.say: Good breast attachment requires four signs: mouth wide open, lower lip curled outward, chin touching breast, and more areola visible above than below. Poor attachment leads to sore nipples.

rows: More areola visible above upper lip
Equal or more areola below lower lip
Nipple pinched at front of mouth
Chin far away from breast tissue

steps.tx: Objective parameters confirm whether an exclusively breastfed infant receives adequate caloric and fluid intake. Reliable indicators of **adequate lactation** include the infant passing clear, pale urine six or more times per twenty-four hours, passing three to four soft yellow stools daily, resting contentedly for two to three hours between feeds, and regaining birth weight by ten to fourteen days of life, followed by steady weight gain of twenty to thirty grams daily.
steps.say: Adequate milk intake is confirmed when the infant produces six or more wet nappies daily, passes yellow seedy stools, sleeps contentedly between feeds, and gains twenty to thirty grams daily.

left.title: Signs of Adequate Intake
points: >=6 wet nappies/day, 3-4 golden stools, audible swallowing during feeds, returns to birth weight by day 10-14

right.title: Signs of Inadequate Intake
points: Weight loss >10% at birth, persistent dark concentrated urine, continuous fretful crying, jaundice progression
